text.p: French first division programme on Thursday and Friday (standings in brackets):

Bastia (3) v Bordeaux (4) Bordeaux, two points behind the home side, will not want to allow Bastia to pull further away in a clash of sides fighting to keep within striking distance of leading duo Monaco and Paris Saint-Germain. Bordeaux's Jean-Pierre Papin is suspended and Ibrahima Ba doubtful, but Johan Micoud returns to midfield, while Bastia's 11-goal striker Anton Drobnjak is back after World Cup duty with Yugoslavia.

Rennes (12) v Marseille (10) Marseille, having confirmed good form with win over Auxerre on Sunday, will be at full strength as they look for first away victory against team with best home record in division -- 26 points in 10 games.

Paris Saint-Germain (2) v Montpellier (17) PSG, after fine performance in 0-0 draw at Nantes, will want to go into winter break on winning note, but will be wary of second successive home upset by relegation haunted side after loss to Nancy at Parc des Princes 11 days ago. Montpellier ended run of six games without victory by beating Lens 1-0 on Saturday.

Lens (16) v Monaco (1) Leaders Monaco face Lens side in crisis after seven league games without victory. Two points ahead, only defeat would allow Monaco's lead to be snatched back by PSG. Monaco glad to play away from their awful Louis II stadium pitch on which they struggled to beat Cannes 1-0 last weekend.
Nice (20) v Lille (13) Nice, surprise 1-0 winners at Guingamp last weekend, will be looking for third win in four games against poor travellers Lille, who have not won in six matches.

Auxerre (5) v Strasbourg (7) Champions play 30th match of season with form and fitness problems evidenced by two successive defeats and six goals conceded in Marseille, including League Cup tie. France defender Alain Goma and midfielder Sabri Lamouchi doubtful, wing Bernard Diomede still unavailable. Strasbourg have lost last two games.

Metz (6) v Caen (18) Caen will be looking to confirm newly-found goal touch after 4-0 home win over Le Havre on Saturday. Metz, 1-0 winners at Strasbourg, appear to have put unlucky UEFA Cup exit to Newcastle United behind them.
Le Havre (14) v Nancy (19) Nancy won their last away game in Paris to topple PSG from top of standings, while Le Havre will be looking for improvement after crashing 4-0 at Caen.

Lyon (8) v Nantes (9) Nantes striker Japhet N'Doram, division's joint top scorer, underwent surgery on troublesome knee on Monday and will miss trip to Lyon. For Lyon, who defend unbeaten home record, Alain Caveglia has recovered from injury in League Cup win over PSG eight days ago, but Polish international defender Jacek Bak is doubtful with leg muscle injury.

Cannes (15) v Guingamp (11) Guingamp, who lost 1-0 at home to bottom club Nice last weekend and want to ensure first division survival above all else, are refusing to part with sought-after France defender Vincent Candela until end of season.
